answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that vests slowly, like a grove that only yields fruit after seasons of care. New accounts wander in with zero reputation and no payout weight until they complete verified work over a long horizon, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs real capital locked for months while earning nothing. Attackers must fund every clone up front, and slashing burns the stake of any identity caught copying or colluding, making mass fakery unprofitable.
